correct_completion: had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
full_sentence: Never before had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
acceptable_variants: had I ever seen such a beautiful sunset.
had I experienced such a beautiful sunset.

options.text: I had seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: After 'never before' the auxiliary must come before the subject, so the inversion 'had I' is required.

options.text: such a beautiful sunset had I seen.
options.why_wrong: Inversion is needed, but the object should stay after the verb; only the auxiliary and subject swap places.

options.text: had I seen such a beautiful sunset.
I have never seen such a beautiful sunset.
options.why_wrong: This has no inversion, and it repeats the negative meaning already given by 'never before'.

explanation: After negative adverbial phrases such as 'never before', English places the auxiliary verb before the subject. Learners whose first language does not use this inversion often keep the normal subject-verb order by mistake.
translation: Nunca antes había visto una puesta de sol tan hermosa.
